proof_review: Wing omission inheritance uses actual support: if a wing omission stayed transitive, the other full wing and q would make the corresponding parent omission transitive. This includes the empty marking on a singleton, with no nonexistent wing omission asserted.

For a nonadjacent right split j, every mark after i+1 fixes b by the acquired unique-crossing lemma. Transitivity of the right wing forces rho_(i+1) to move b, so b belongs to its near side C. The parent j-omission contains transitive groups on A,C,D and q joins A,C. Any q-edge C to D would make that omission transitive. As q has only its original A-to-B crossing, q consequently preserves D.

Commutation of q and rho_j, and uniqueness of the rho_j edge between D and its complement, makes q fix c,d separately. Since q centralizes the tail transitive on D, q fixes all D. A singleton D needs only its setwise preservation. The new parent split has exact sides A union C,D; rho_j fixes A, so a trivial internal factor is preserved. No terminal-tail transitivity on more than one point is assumed.

At the adjacent first wing split, its near side is a singleton. The tail fixes b, so b is that singleton unless D is also a singleton, when the labels may be chosen accordingly. The restriction beta of q to D centralizes its transitive tail T. A nonidentity such involution is fixed-point-free; its actual two-point orbits are invariant under T.

Choose a minimal subfamily M of the specified T marks transitive on these actual pairs. The acquired forest proof bounds its size by |D|/2-1. On D, the group generated by M and q is transitive: M moves pairs transitively, while the single simultaneous involution beta interchanges the two points of every pair. Individual independent pair flips are not required.

Adding all left marks and rho_j makes the actual full-domain action transitive. Thus every specified T mark must be present in M, or its parent maximal omission would be transitive. The resulting t-1<=|M|<=|D|/2-1 contradicts the exact hypothesis 2t>m-1. Hence beta is trivial, and the new split has trivial near factor because rho_j fixes A and only moves b across the cut.

Reversal gives the left-hand conclusions. No connected-diagram, group-rank classification, parity assumption or projected intersection property is silently added. Neither theorem establishes the existence of an internal wing split or the full stability correspondence.
